outcome: Nothing found since 26 January 2024 settles, restricts or moves the question. For the Henson graphs H_n (n ≥ 3) the finite model property of the first-order theory is still listed as unsolved on Wikipedia, and the most specific status source I found (Kruckman, arXiv 1510.03539, v2 2018, published 2019) records that it is unknown whether the theory of the triangle-free Henson graph H_3 is pseudofinite. The 2026 Henson-graph papers I found concern other properties (big Ramsey degrees, chromatic number, the finite length property) or a different logic.
problem_asks: (1) Scope: 'the Henson graphs', meaning the countable homogeneous K_n-free graphs H_n (Henson 1971) for every n ≥ 3, with H_3 the triangle-free generic graph. The bullet does not restrict n, so it asks about all of them together; a result for H_3 alone would leave every H_n with n ≥ 4 open, and the reverse. (2) Property: 'the finite model property'. The bullet names no logic. Read as first-order logic, which fits the Wikipedia link target (the general finite model property article) and the form of Cherlin's question as recorded in the sources I found: for each H_n, every consistent first-order sentence of its theory Th(H_n) has a finite model. For a complete theory with infinite models this is the same as Th(H_n) being pseudofinite. (3) The bullet could also be read as the stronger finite submodel property (every first-order sentence true in H_n holds in some finite substructure of H_n); it does not say which, and I have recorded results on both readings where they appear.

events.what_happened: Alex Kruckman (UC Berkeley), 'Amalgamation and the finite model property', slides dated 25 March 2015, hosted on his Wesleyan page. I could not decode the PDF, so this rests on search excerpts of its first slides. The excerpts say the talk takes Cherlin's question (from Cherlin's 'Exercises for logicians') as its starting point: when does a homogeneous structure in a finite relational language have the finite model property? They also list 'Cherlin's Question (Open)': does the theory of the generic triangle-free graph have the finite model property? It predates the window and records the question as open; it is not a result.
events.delivers: Nothing established. It states the question for the generic triangle-free graph (H_3) and frames a research programme: rule out algebraic and stability-based sources of the FMP, then argue that the remaining purely combinatorial cases are explained by randomness. The talk says that if this worked, the generic triangle-free graph would answer Cherlin's question negatively. That is a strategy, not a proof.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, for every H_n with n ≥ 3.
events.time_since_posted: over 11 years as of October 2026, with no resolution I could find
events.direction: Records the question as open. Does not cut either way on the answer.

events.what_happened: Alex Kruckman, 'Disjoint n-amalgamation and pseudofinite countably categorical theories', arXiv:1510.03539 (v1 submitted 13 Oct 2015; v2 revised 17 Sep 2018; journal reference Notre Dame J. Formal Logic 60(1) (2019), 139-160). The paper shows that a countably categorical theory with an expansion having disjoint n-amalgamation for all n is pseudofinite, extends this by filtrations of Fraïssé classes to some non-simple theories (generic equivalence-relation theories), and states in §1 that 'it is still unknown whether the theory of the generic triangle-free graph is pseudofinite'. In §4.1 it says 'this method cannot be used to show that the theory of the generic triangle-free graph is pseudofinite'.
events.revisions: v1 13 Oct 2015; v2 17 Sep 2018 (minor, 'to appear in Notre Dame J. Formal Logic'); published NDJFL 60(1) 2019.
events.delivers: Establishes pseudofiniteness, hence the finite model property, for countably categorical theories with an expansion having disjoint n-amalgamation for all n, and for two generic theories of equivalence relations. Establishes nothing about any Henson graph. It says the method fails for the triangle-free graph, and says the generic triangle-free graph has SOP3 but NSOP4. The parts I read do not treat H_n for n ≥ 4.
events.remains: The pseudofiniteness (FMP) of Th(H_n) for every n ≥ 3. The paper states the triangle-free case H_3 open. Its status for H_n with n ≥ 4 is not discussed in the parts I read.

checked_by.who: Notre Dame Journal of Formal Logic (refereed journal)
checked_by.qualification: Journal of record in mathematical logic
checked_by.what_they_did: Refereed and published the paper, which proves its own results. It did not address the Henson question, which the paper leaves open.

events.direction: A barrier statement for H_3. It records the question as open and says its own method cannot settle it, so it cuts neither way on the answer.

events.what_happened: Gabriel Conant and Alex Kruckman, 'Three surprising instances of dividing', arXiv:2311.00609 (v1 submitted 1 Nov 2023; v2 4 Apr 2024, minor revisions; listed as to appear in JSL, later dated volume 91 issue 3, September 2026). It gives three counterexamples to a folklore claim about extending types over algebraic closures and dividing versus forking, an NSOP1 theory where a type forks but does not divide, and consequences for free-amalgamation theories and generic K_{m,n}-free incidence structures. The abstract page does not mention Henson graphs, the finite model property, pseudofinite theories or triangle-free graphs.
events.revisions: v1 1 Nov 2023; v2 4 Apr 2024 (minor, in window); journal volume dated September 2026 per the author's page.
events.delivers: Results on forking and dividing in NSOP1 and free-amalgamation theories. Not about finite models, pseudofiniteness, or Henson graphs as far as the abstract shows.
events.direction: Does not bear on the finite model property. Cuts neither way.

events.what_happened: Gábor Sági, 'On the finite submodel property', Set Theory Seminar talk at the Rényi Institute, listed as 2 October 2025. The abstract surveys adapting the measure argument that the Rado graph has the finite submodel property to certain homogeneous structures. It states two results: a new sufficient condition for a stable structure to have the finite submodel property, and a partial converse, that for certain structures the property yields automorphism-invariant probability measures on definable relations. The abstract does not mention Henson graphs or triangle-free graphs. I found no written paper or arXiv preprint for it.
events.delivers: Stated results concern stable structures (a sufficient condition for the finite submodel property) and a converse linking that property to invariant measures. Nothing stated about the Henson graphs. The finite submodel property, every first-order formula true in the structure holds in a finite substructure, implies FMP for the theory, so a positive result of this kind would bear on the question. The abstract gives no application to Henson graphs.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, for every H_n. The Henson theories are unstable (Kruckman: the generic triangle-free graph has SOP3), so the stable-case condition does not reach them on its face. I have not checked the exact hypotheses against a paper, because none was found.
events.time_since_posted: about 12 months as of October 2026, with no write-up found
events.direction: Neither way on the Henson question. It is a related but different result, for stable structures.

events.what_happened: Jingjie Yang, Mikołaj Bojańczyk and Bartek Klin, 'The Finite Length Property of the Rado Graph and Friends', arXiv:2605.21681 (v1 20 May 2026; v2 9 Jul 2026). The paper defines a 'finite length property' (for each finite power of the structure, chains of equivariant subspaces in the associated free vector space over a field are bounded in length). Theorem 30 proves it for Fraïssé limits of free-amalgamation classes in a finite vocabulary of at most binary relations. In the HTML I read, Fact 69 (Appendix D) lists 'Henson's K_n-free graph, where n ≥ 3' among the countable homogeneous graphs, and Claim 70 states 'All countable homogeneous graphs have the finite length property over any field'. The terms 'finite model property', 'finite submodel property' and 'pseudofinite' do not appear in the parts I read. The earlier September 2026 record for this problem says this paper does not mention Henson graphs; the HTML I read contradicts that.
events.revisions: v1 20 May 2026; v2 9 Jul 2026 (per arXiv abstract page).
events.delivers: A different property. The finite length property, not the finite model property, holds for every countable homogeneous graph, which includes every Henson graph H_n with n ≥ 3 (Claim 70 as read). It says nothing about finite models or about first-order theories, so it neither establishes nor moves the FMP for any H_n.
events.remains: All of problem_asks. The finite model property of Th(H_n) is not addressed.
events.direction: Neither way on FMP. It is a result on a neighbouring, algebraic property that holds for every Henson graph. Easy to conflate with FMP by keyword (a 'finite ... property' of Henson and Rado graphs).

events.what_happened: Peter Cholak, Natasha Dobrinen and Charlie McCoy, 'The Henson graphs: colorings and codings', arXiv:2604.09894 (math.LO; v1 10 Apr 2026; v2 1 May 2026, minor changes). The abstract states exact finite big Ramsey degrees for finite graphs G in the universal K_{n+1}-free graph H_{n+1}, a computable colouring bound, and that for some colourings every computable copy computes the halting set. It does not mention the finite model property, pseudofinite theories or first-order finite models.
events.delivers: Big Ramsey degrees and colouring results for the Henson graphs. Not about finite models. Nothing stated establishes FMP for any H_n.
events.direction: Neither way on FMP. A different property of the same family of graphs.

events.what_happened: Peter Cholak, Natasha Dobrinen and Henry Towsner, 'The finite big Ramsey degrees of Henson graphs are provable in ACA_0', arXiv:2606.30885 (v1 29 Jun 2026). The abstract states that the finite big Ramsey degree statement for Henson graphs is provable in ACA_0' and, with the earlier Cholak–Dobrinen–McCoy result, equivalent to ACA_0' over RCA_0. It does not mention the finite model property or pseudofinite theories.
events.delivers: A reverse-mathematics result on big Ramsey degrees of Henson graphs. Not about finite models.

events.what_happened: Hirotaka Kikyo, Koitaro Nakaura and Akito Tsuboi, 'On chromatic number of countable graphs', arXiv:2602.20667 (math.LO; submitted 24 Feb 2026). The abstract says that for Fraïssé limits instability forces infinite chromatic number, that this yields a classification of homogeneous graphs with finite chromatic number, and that Hrushovski constructions have finite chromatic number. The abstract does not name Henson graphs or the finite model property.
events.delivers: Chromatic numbers of countable graphs and Fraïssé limits. Not about finite models. Whether the classification covers the Henson graphs in the way it is stated, I did not check beyond the abstract.

events.what_happened: Oskar Fiuk, 'Random Models and the Guarded Fragment', arXiv:2601.05247 (v1 8 Jan 2026; v2 28 May 2026). It gives a new probabilistic proof that the Guarded Fragment of first-order logic has the finite model property, with a doubly exponential bound on minimal models, extended to the Triguarded Fragment and derandomised. The term 'finite model property' is used here for a different logic. It does not mention Henson graphs, pseudofinite theories or triangle-free graphs.
events.delivers: The finite model property for the Guarded Fragment and Triguarded Fragment, which are different logics and classes of sentences from the first-order theories of the Henson graphs. Establishes nothing about H_n.
events.direction: Does not bear on the question. It is a same-named property in a different logic, so it cuts neither way.

events.what_happened: Peter J. Cameron, 'Around homogeneity', arXiv:2602.22181 (math.CO; submitted 25 Feb 2026). It recounts Woodrow's homogeneous triangle-free graph and its place in the history of homogeneous structures, and suggests that Fraïssé classes of rigid structures may generalise Ramsey classes. The abstract page does not mention Henson graphs, H_3, pseudofinite structures, the finite model property or Cherlin.
events.delivers: Historical and expository material on homogeneous triangle-free graphs. Establishes nothing about finite models.

summary: Nothing I could establish has settled or moved the question since 26 January 2024. I read the bullet as asking whether Th(H_n) has the finite model property for each Henson graph H_n with n ≥ 3, H_3 included, with the first-order reading preferred because the Wikipedia link goes to the general FMP article and Cherlin's question, as recorded in the sources, is about first-order theories of homogeneous structures. The Wikipedia unsolved-problem box (opened; undated) still lists it. The most specific status evidence is Kruckman, arXiv:1510.03539 (2015; v2 2018; NDJFL 2019), which says it is unknown whether the theory of the generic triangle-free graph is pseudofinite and that its disjoint n-amalgamation method cannot show it. I found no later source that resolves it. Kruckman's research page lists no pseudofinite paper after 2019, and his 2026 entry is on dividing. Bodirsky–Jahel (arXiv:2204.01404, v3 June 2024) calls a directed-graph analogue 'wide open' but does not mention the Henson question. A search snippet for García–Robles (arXiv:2309.00991, 2023) says it names the triangle-free case as open; I could not confirm this from the abstract page, and it predates the window anyway. The attribution to Cherlin rests on search snippets of Kruckman's 2015 slides and Chernikov's 2019 UCLA notes, because both PDFs could not be decoded. The in-window Henson-graph papers do not bear on the question: big Ramsey degrees (Cholak–Dobrinen–McCoy, April 2026; Cholak–Dobrinen–Towsner, June 2026), chromatic number (Kikyo et al., February 2026), a survey (Cameron, February 2026), and the finite model property for the Guarded Fragment (Fiuk, January 2026, a different logic). A Rényi talk by Sági (2 October 2025) on the finite submodel property for stable structures does not name Henson graphs. Yang–Bojańczyk–Klin (May 2026) do cover every countable homogeneous graph, including every Henson graph, but for the finite length property, which is a different algebraic notion. The earlier September 2026 record for this problem says that paper does not mention Henson graphs; the HTML I read contradicts it. Close calls: the Sági talk and the Yang et al. paper could be read as neighbouring progress. Against that, neither states anything about FMP or about Th(H_n). The Henson theories are unstable (Kruckman: the generic triangle-free graph has SOP3), so Sági's stable-case condition does not reach them on its face; I have not checked the hypotheses against a paper, because none was found. The AI search found no system connected to this problem. OpenAI's 1 August 2026 'Ten advances' report (Astra) is the only large 2026 AI-mathematics announcement I found that could touch model theory. Its official page returned HTTP 403, and secondary reports list results in geometry, coding theory, group theory and combinatorics. None is described as model-theoretic, but the list I could reconstruct is partial and I could not verify it against the primary source.
competing_reading: Read 'finite model property' as the stronger finite submodel property and 'the Henson graphs' as the whole family. On that reading the Sági talk (October 2025) and the Yang et al. finite length result (May 2026, every countable homogeneous graph) could be counted as neighbouring progress toward the bullet, and the question would look less settled by the old Kruckman barrier. The case against: neither result states the finite submodel property or FMP for any Henson graph; Yang et al. concern a different algebraic property; and the Kruckman barrier is about H_3 only, so it leaves H_n for n ≥ 4 open either way. A second competing reading is that Kruckman's 2019 method might settle some H_n, n ≥ 4, which the paper's parts I read do not state.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or published paper proving or refuting pseudofiniteness (equivalently FMP for the complete theory) of Th(H_3), which would settle the triangle-free case and resolve the 2015 Cherlin question; or one covering every H_n with n ≥ 3. Also: a write-up of the Sági talk stating the hypotheses and whether they cover any Henson graph; the Kruckman Torino lecture notes (May/June 2025), which may restate the status; Cherlin's 'Exercises for logicians' (sites.math.rutgers.edu/~cherlin/Problems/exercises.pdf), which may be the question's original statement; and a readable copy of the OpenAI 'Ten advances' manuscript list, to confirm that no item concerns model theory.

judgement.why: No event establishes or bounds the finite model property for any Henson graph. The three pre-snapshot events record the question as open (Kruckman's 2019 journal paper proves results for other theories and states a barrier for H_3); none settles part of the statement, so scope none. The post-snapshot events concern other properties of the same graphs (big Ramsey degrees, chromatic number, exposition: none) or same-sounding properties in a different setting (Sági's finite submodel property for stable structures, the finite length property, FMP for the Guarded Fragment: variant). Sági's talk and Yang–Bojańczyk–Klin were the closest calls; neither states anything about Th(H_n) or finite models of it, and the Henson theories are unstable, so variant is the right reading. No AI involvement was found for any event.
judgement.doubts: Several status sources (Kruckman 2015 slides, Cherlin's notes, Kruckman's Dec 2025 lecture notes) were seen only through search excerpts, and Sági's talk has no write-up, so its hypotheses were not checked against the Henson graphs. The OpenAI 'Ten advances' list was reconstructed only from secondary reports.
